Subject: OpsAI inference evaluation — call recap + initial cost baseline

Hi Alex — thanks for taking the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Recap of what OpsAI said on the call:
- Primary app: realtime inference for policy scoring (99th pct latency target ~120ms).
- Expected volume: steady 200 requests/sec with short bursts to 1k rps; average payload ~400 tokens in, ~120 tokens out.
- Key evaluation asks: (1) direct perf/cost comparison vs Hyperscaler A endpoints, (2) clear per-1M-token economics with batching and cache assumptions, (3) guidance on isolation (dedicated) vs hosted.

Initial Redwood baseline (back-of-envelope we discussed):
- Per-1M tokens (in+out) estimate: $22–$28 depending on batching and KV cache hit-rate.
- Typical levers: batch size (1/8/16), session cache hit-rate (0/40/80%), and reserved capacity for predictable throughput.

Proposed next tests (what we can run quickly):
1) Micro-bench: per-1M token cost at batch sizes [1, 8, 16], 1M token sample workload (your payload distribution).
2) Cache sensitivity: measure token cost with 0%, 40%, and 80% KV-prefix hit rates.
3) Latency SLO sweep: 99th pct at small batch sizes (1 and 8) to verify 120ms target under 200 rps.

What I need from you to get started:
- Sample payloads (400 tokens in typical, and top 5 outliers).
- Confirmation whether the ephemeral KV cache is representative of a session cache or if you expect cross-session reuse.

If you can share the sample prompts and any desired SLAs I’ll loop in engineering and we’ll schedule a focused run next week.

Best,

Thanks Sofia — appreciated the summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: 99th pct target is firm at 120ms for global users; p50/p90 can be higher but p99 is critical for our monitoring.
- Volume profile: the 200 rps steady is accurate; bursts will be short (30–45s) but frequent during business hours.
- Cache behavior: roughly ~40% reuse for session-level KV; certain customers (enterprise) will have higher reuse (~70–80%) for identical prompts.

I attached a procurement-focused TCO spreadsheet that includes expected request mix and our internal cost target — we're hoping to see Redwood get us under $25/1M tokens as a baseline with obvious optimizations.

Next steps on our side: we’ll upload sample_prompts.json and a small synthetic traffic replay for you to use. Can you confirm what format you prefer? JSONL of prompts with metadata is fine.
